title: Where does an archetype's example content come from, and which settings must an author supply?
description: ST-DECL-UC01-R01 and R04 say each archetype supplies the smallest example content that checking accepts, and R05 says an empty scaffold names every setting the author must supply. Today the scaffolds of rpc-service and browser-service are refused: rpc-service needs the grpc-processes settings processes and proto_files, a proto file and a process factory package (factory/rpc.go) that imports the generated packages by the module path; browser-service needs a distinct api_prefix. The Archetype entity (ST-SUP-EN03) has no field that holds example content, and a component schema marks as required both settings the declaration must give and settings that only the running service gets (such as connection_string of postgres-adapter and issuer of jwt-auth), so checking cannot tell which settings an author must supply. Options: (a) add to the Archetype an example content field (files under the archetype folder and the settings to write into the declaration, with the module path as a placeholder), and mark in a component schema each setting the declaration must give, so that checking refuses its absence and init can name it; (b) keep the example content in Declaring's code, one case per archetype; (c) narrow R01, R04 and R05 to archetypes that can be empty, such as rest-crud. Recommendation: (a), since the UC01 notes say the archetype supplies its example content, and a registry change then needs no change to STEGO's code. Until then UC01-R01, R04-T01, R05 and the flow test stay not automated; rest-crud, which can be empty, already passes as written.

title: Which step of Record what a service was built from fulfills that apply writes the record inside the service's repo?
description: ST-GEN-UC01-R05 says that apply MUST write the record inside the service's repo, beside the code it generated. Only the step ST-GEN-UC01-FL-S02 (the service author commits the record with the generated code) fulfills it, and that step invokes no command, so no technical record can build the requirement, although ST-GEN-UC01-R05-T01 is automated and passes. Options: (a) ST-GEN-UC01-FL-S01, which invokes Apply a plan (ST-GEN-CMD01), also fulfills ST-GEN-UC01-R05, and S02 keeps it too; (b) S02 also invokes Apply a plan; (c) the requirement stays proved and not built. Recommendation: (a), since apply is what writes the record in the repo and the commit only shows it.

title: What writes the emitted authorization schema to SpiceDB?
description: ST-SUP-RC29-OC13 says the generator MUST NOT write the schema to the provider at generation, and ST-DECL-INV22 says the generator adds the floor marker definition to the schema it writes. The spicedb-authz generator now emits the schema with the marker as the constant Schema and the file internal/authz/schema.zed, and the relay's start-up check refuses to start on a provider whose schema lacks the marker. Nothing writes the schema to the provider: the runtime library has no schema write (stego.dev/runtime/authz calls WriteRelationships, CheckPermission and LookupResources only), and the deployment component has no step for it. Options: (a) the deployment writes schema.zed with zed schema write, or a job of the release, before the new version starts; (b) the authorization runtime gives WriteSchema(ctx, conn, schema), and the service calls it at start-up before the relay's check, which needs a provider key that may write the schema; (c) the operator writes it by hand. Recommendation: (a), because the schema is a release artifact that the service source holds, a schema change can then be reviewed and rolled back with the release, and the service key needs no schema write. Until it is decided, the tests write the emitted Schema to a local SpiceDB as the deployment would.

title: Where does the relay's watch read the oldest age of the authz outbox messages?
description: ST-SUP-RP06-LC14 says the relay MUST raise one alert on each upward crossing of outbox.oldest.age{destination=authz} past the delivery alert bound. authz.Relay.Watch(ctx, interval, oldest) takes the reader as a function, OldestAge. The outbox runtime gives the oldest age only as the observable gauge of the worker's meter; its read of the relay function stego_outbox.oldest is unexported. So the service must read its own metric back through a reader of the meter provider, which the runtime's tests and the generated wiring's test do, and which depends on how the service exports metrics. The reader is the same for every declaration, so ST-STD-RUNTIME-R05 puts it in the runtime library, and a builder of generators must not change runtime behaviour. Options: (a) the outbox runtime gives Worker.OldestAge(ctx, destination) (time.Duration, error) over the same relay function, which the generated wiring passes to Watch; (b) the authorization runtime reads the gauge through a metric reader that the service gives; (c) the generator emits the reader. Recommendation: (a), because it reads the same source as the gauge and needs no metric pipeline. Until it is decided, the emitted Watch takes an OldestAge from the caller, and the service's main does not run it yet.
